chapter: Arrangers, Bill Robinson and Coleman Hawkins
title: Recording four tunes for Joe Davis with Coleman Hawkins
summary: Thomas hires Hawkins for a hundred dollars a day, writes progressions for four tunes, and finds he reads the piano part.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Coleman Hawkins and the great saxophonists

blocks.x: I had the privilege of making... See, Joe Davis asked me if I could get Coleman... I had nerve. I

said, "Well, I'll check it out." So I called Coleman. I said, "Coleman, would you do a recording date with me?' He said, "Yeah." I said, "How much you want?" He said, "I'll do it for a hundred dollars a day." Well, that was so cheap, I think I told him "yeah" then. I didn't even check with Joe Davis, but I knowed that would be all right. And that's when I got him after Ben Webster. Because I was always changing my personnel.

Then after he did the date with me, we made a date with just him... I wish I could get ahold of them records. I wrote four tunes for him. And all I did was write the progressions. See, because he was a master at progression. And me being a saxophone player, I knew the different progressions that saxophone players like. They love the modulation of the fifth, and they can go into any change and go into the fifth. So I just made different changes... And one thing I give Joe Davis credit for, he could give a name to a tune. I had Monk on piano, I forget what the rest of the session... That's the only name I remember.

And so we got to the date. And Coleman says, "Where's the piano part?" Now, I had all the chords on his sheet. He said, "Where is the piano part?" I gave him the piano part. He went to the... That's the first time I knew he played piano. He went to the piano, and he said, "Let's
go." And he could go in there and take his first take. His first take was a masterpiece...

But see, I found out from all of them saxophone players, Chu Berry, Ben Webster, Coleman Hawkins, they had all their set things that they just knew by memory. And they could ad-lib from one chord to another just like you and I talking. And he went over them chords from the piano... And I had them on his sheet, but he wanted to get the piano. And that's when I found out he played piano. And he said, "Let's go." And he didn't have to go to learn a tune but a couple of times, and he had it.
